Maria (PM): Heads up — competitor X just announced an "enterprise routing" product: region-aware model routing + automated fallback to cheaper variants. They’re pitching it as an easy migration for enterprise apps. :eyes:
Kevin (Eng): Saw that. Sounds like a mix of smart routing + model variants + policy layer. We already have routing and variants but not packaged as a single enterprise feature.
Sasha (Growth PM): We’ve had 3 inbound requests this quarter asking for simpler routing + SLA mapping to models. Sales says it's a recurring ask for mid-market accounts.
Noah (ML Research): From an infra perspective, the main gap is the admin UX to define routing policies and strong telemetry tying routing decisions to SLA/KPI. We have pieces: smart routing, fallbacks, policy engine prototype.
Maria (PM): Proposal: small initiative: "Enterprise Routing Pack" — 3-month timeline, MVP includes: policy UI, rule-based routing by region/tier/latency, automatic fallback to pinned model variant, and audit logs. Launch criteria: can route 95% of requests without manual ops, telemetry surfaces cost/latency delta per policy.
Kevin (Eng): Engineering note: to hit 3 months we need to scope down. Recommend backend + API + basic UI. No A/B rollout in MVP. Also need feature flags for canary.
Ali (Design): I can sketch policy flows + card UI for rule creation in 2 sprints. Keep UX minimal: domain + condition + fallback target.
Sasha (Growth PM): Minimum customer ask: VPC + KMS integration remains separate (Private product) but we should ensure routing policies are compatible with Dedicated/Private.
Noah (ML Research): Risk: automatic fallback could change quality; we need guardrails. Suggest mandatory evaluation set for each customer to detect regressions, and an opt-in labelling of fallbacks in responses.
Kevin (Eng): Agree on guardrails. Implementation sketch:
```
policy: {
  match: { region: 'eu', tier: 'gold' },
  primary: 'redwood/gpt-3.5-rt',
  fallback: 'redwood/gpt-3.5-cost',
  max_latency_ms: 250
}
```
We can store policies in config service, evaluate at routing layer.
Maria (PM): Can we create a simple launch checklist? I’ll start: 1) Policy CRUD API, 2) UI for creating policies, 3) Telemetry showing cost/latency delta per policy, 4) Fallback audit logs, 5) Canaries for 10% traffic, 6) Regression alerting for quality.
Kevin (Eng): Swap 5) to post-MVP unless sales needs it immediately. For MVP, implement a toggle to enable policy at workspace level and allow manual test mode.
Sasha (Growth PM): Sales feedback: if we can demo region-based routing + a clear SLA-to-model mapping in a week or two, it will unlock one pilot. So the MVP must be demoable.
Ali (Design): For demo we can build a lightweight policy builder and a demo workspace with example traffic. That keeps scope small.
Noah (ML Research): For regression alerts we can re-use eval infra but add a lightweight scoring hook to flag >5% divergence for key prompts. That can be deferred but wire the hook now.
Maria (PM): Prioritization: must-have: policy API, routing integration, fallback mechanism, telemetry events. Nice-to-have: multi-tenant UI, automated rollout %, KMS/VPC entanglement.
Kevin (Eng): Rough estimate: backend + routing integration 6-7 dev-weeks, telemetry 2w, UI 3w (design + frontend), QA 1-2w. With 2 engs + 1 infra, 3 months seems tight but doable if we cut rollout automation.
Sasha (Growth PM): Commercial angle: call it "Routing Controls for Enterprise". Price as add-on for Dedicated/Private customers + self-serve limited version for Hosted.
Noah (ML Research): Also propose a policy preset library: low-latency, cost-optimized, quality-first. These presets make sales demos quick.
Maria (PM): Action items: Kevin — confirm eng estimates & infra dependencies by EOD Friday. Ali — first demo mocks by next Tue. Sasha — identify 1 pilot account willing to test demo. Noah — list 5 eval prompts for guardrails. I’ll draft PRD and rollout plan.
ops-bot: deploy-notice: staging routing-service v0.42 deployed by kevin at 2001234600.
Kevin (Eng): quick follow-up — we need to decide fallback semantics: hard-fallback (switch model) vs hybrid (try primary, if latency > threshold stream fallback). Hybrid is more complex. MVP: hard-fallback.
Sasha (Growth PM): Hard-fallback is fine for demo. Make sure response headers include which model served the request for audit.
Noah (ML Research): Add explicit metadata field: "served_by" and "fallback_reason". Useful for both audit + eval sampling.
Maria (PM): Good. I’ll include those in the PRD. If everyone OK, I’ll mark this as "priority" for next planning sprint and loop in Legal for any SLA language changes. :+1:
Kevin (Eng): 👍
Sasha (Growth PM): :rocket:
Ali (Design): :white_check_mark:
Noah (ML Research): :eyes:
Maria (PM): Thanks team — will post PRD link when ready.
